A speed–time graph is plotted for the motion of a car.
Which quantity does the area under the speed–time graph represent?
Which quantity is an example of a force?

A car travels at constant speed along a straight road that has a slight downwards slope.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: There is a resultant force on the car down the slope.
There is a resultant force on the car up the slope.
There is a resultant force on the car vertically downwards.
There is no resultant force on the car.

questions.questionText:
Which energy resource requires a power station with a boiler to produce steam when generating
electricity?

A scientist heats a solid substance until it turns into a liquid, and then into a gas.
Which row describes the two changes of state of the substance as it is heated?
change of state 1 change of state 2

Gases can be compressed, but liquids cannot be compressed.
Which statement explains this difference?

options.text: Each particle in a gas is more compressible than each particle in a liquid.
Particles in a gas are further apart than particles in a liquid.
Particles in a gas attract each other more strongly than particles in a liquid.
Particles in a gas move more slowly than particles in a liquid.

questions.questionText:
A fixed mass of gas at a constant temperature is trapped in a cylinder which has a movable
piston.
Which row states and explains what happens to the pressure of the gas in the cylinder when the
volume of the gas increases?
pressure explanation

options.text: decreases gas particles collide with the cylinder at a lower speed
decreases gas particles collide with the cylinder less frequently
increases gas particles collide with the cylinder at a higher speed
increases gas particles collide with the cylinder more frequently

questions.questionText: Which quantity does not change when there is an increase in temperature?

options.text: the density of a steel block
the diameter of the hole in a metal nut
the length of an iron rod
the mass of a metal coin

questions.questionText:
A person holds an empty glass beaker and pours hot water into it.
Why does it take a few seconds before his hand starts to feel hot?

options.text: Glass is a poor thermal conductor.
Water is a poor thermal conductor.
Glass is a better thermal conductor than water.
Water is a better thermal conductor than glass.

questions.questionText:
A liquid is heated and it expands.
How does this lead to the formation of a convection current?

options.text: The density of the heated liquid decreases.
The density of the heated liquid increases.
The mass of the heated liquid particles decreases.
The mass of the heated liquid particles increases.

questions.questionText:
Some electric hotplates are metal and do not glow when hot.
Other hotplates are glass and have a heater underneath that glows red. The heater makes the
glass hot.
With both hotplates, there is no air gap between the hotplate and a metal pan placed on the
hotplate.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: The glass hotplate transfers less energy by radiation to the base of the pan than the metal hotplate.
The glass hotplate transfers energy by convection to the base of the pan.
The metal hotplate transfers energy by conduction to the base of the pan.
The metal hotplate transfers energy by convection to the base of the pan.

questions.questionText:
A glass rod is rubbed with a silk cloth. The glass rod becomes positively charged.
Which statement explains how this happens?

options.text: Negative charges move from the glass rod to the silk cloth.
Negative charges move from the silk cloth to the glass rod.
Positive charges move from the glass rod to the silk cloth.
